title: API reference and architecture
text: package combines three classical analytical machineries historically sit separate corners literature: phase-space reconstruction delay embedding (Takens 1981; Cao 1997), multivariate empirical mode decomposition (MEMD; Rehman & Mandic 2010) extreme-value theory (EVT) dynamical-systems extremes (Faranda, Lucarini, Turchetti, Vaienti 2011; Lucarini et al. 2016). combination diagnoses chameleon attractors: systems whose effective EVT signature (local dimension, extremal index) varies systematically frequency scale, signalling regime mixing. Three principles govern architecture: first scale separation MEMD. user-supplied multivariate signal decomposed intrinsic mode functions aligned hyperspherical projection directions (Rehman-Mandic). Partial sums frequency cutoff reconstruct scale-filtered signals. second EVT-per-scale fingerprint. local dimension extremal index estimated per scale via peaks--threshold recurrence statistic -log(distance_to_x). two statistics, plotted scale, chameleon fingerprint. third surrogate-based hypothesis testing. null hypothesis “EVT statistics scale-independent” tested one four surrogate methods (scale_shuffle, fourier, iaaft, block_bootstrap); p-values corrected multiple comparisons (Fisher, Bonferroni, BH FDR).

title: Statistical hypothesis testing for chameleon behaviour
text: Visual inspection scale-dependent metrics \(D(f)\) \(\theta(f)\) can suggest chameleon behavior, insufficient rigorous scientific conclusions [1]. Several issues arise: sampling variability means even scale-invariant systems produce non-constant profiles due finite-sample effects; multiple comparisons across many frequency scales make spurious patterns likely chance; arbitrary thresholds leave unclear level variation constitutes “chameleon” behavior; effect magnitude considerations remind us statistical significance imply practical importance. chameleon package provides surrogate-based permutation tests [2] address concerns, yielding p-values effect sizes principled inference.
code: library(chamaeleon) library(knitr) library(ggplot2)

title: Statistical hypothesis testing for chameleon behaviour
text: null hypothesis states \(D(f)\) \(\theta(f)\) constant across frequency scales: \[H_0: D(f_1) = D(f_2) = \cdots = D(f_K)\] \[H_0: \theta(f_1) = \theta(f_2) = \cdots = \theta(f_K)\] \(H_0\), observed variation due sampling noise, genuine scale-dependent dynamics.

title: Statistical hypothesis testing for chameleon behaviour
text: alternative hypothesis states least one metric varies systematically scale: \[H_1: D(f) \text{ /} \theta(f) \text{ vary } f\]

title: Statistical hypothesis testing for chameleon behaviour
text: primary testing method scale shuffling [2]: randomly permute frequency labels computed metrics. preserves marginal distributions \(D\) \(\theta\) breaking systematic relationship scale. surrogate, procedure involves randomly reordering \(K\) frequency labels, computing test statistics shuffled data, comparing observed statistics null distribution. directly tests whether metrics depend scale ordering.

title: Statistical hypothesis testing for chameleon behaviour
text: Uses conservative formula Phipson & Smyth (2010) [3]: \[p = \frac{\sum_{=1}^{B} (|T_i^*| \geq |T_{obs}|) + 1}{B + 1}\] avoids \(p = 0\) provides valid permutation p-values.

text: chameleon attractor strange attractor whose geometric topological properties vary dynamically across time frequency scales [1]. Unlike traditional attractors fixed global properties, chameleon attractors adapt characteristics depending observational scale, revealing fundamentally different dynamics different frequencies. chameleon package implements multiscale dynamical systems analysis detecting characterizing chameleon attractors. methodology combines three theoretical pillars: Takens embedding theorem phase-space reconstruction [2]; multivariate empirical mode decomposition (MEMD) scale separation [3]; extreme value theory (EVT) computing instantaneous dynamical metrics [4]. vignette provides complete mathematical theory underlying package, based Alberti et al. (2023) [1].

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: Given univariate time series \(\Theta(t)\) observed dynamical system, Takens’ theorem (1981) [2] guarantees generic conditions, original attractor can reconstructed via delay embedding: \[\Theta(t) \rightarrow \mathbf{\Theta}_{m,\Delta}(t) = \left[\Theta(t), \Theta(t-\Delta), \Theta(t-2\Delta), \ldots, \Theta(t-(m-1)\Delta)\right]^\top\] \(m\) embedding dimension \(\Delta\) time delay (samples). theorem states original system attractor dimension \(D\), choosing \(m > 2D\) guarantees diffeomorphic (topology-preserving) reconstruction.

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: Time delay estimation uses autocorrelation function (ACF): \[\Delta = \min\{k : \rho_k < 0.5\}\] \(\rho_k = \mathrm{ACF}(k)\) autocorrelation lag \(k\). Alternative criteria include first minimum mutual information [5]. Embedding dimension estimation uses false nearest neighbors (FNN) method [6]. dimension \(m\), find nearest neighbor point check remains neighbor dimension \(m+1\). false neighbor satisfies either: \[\frac{|x_{+m\Delta} - x_{j+m\Delta}|}{\|\mathbf{x}_i^{(m)} - \mathbf{x}_j^{(m)}\|} > R_{\mathrm{tol}}\] \[|x_{+m\Delta} - x_{j+m\Delta}| > A_{\mathrm{tol}} \cdot \sigma_x\] \(R_{\mathrm{tol}} \approx 15\) \(A_{\mathrm{tol}} \approx 2\) tolerance parameters.

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: empirical mode decomposition (EMD) [7] decomposes signal intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) iterative sifting process. univariate signal \(x(t)\): \[x(t) = \sum_{k=1}^{N} c_k(t) + r(t)\] \(c_k(t)\) IMF satisfying two conditions: number extrema zero crossings differ one, mean upper lower envelopes zero points.

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: multivariate signal \(\mathbf{\Theta}_\mu(t) \\mathbb{R}^p\), MEMD [3] projects signal onto \(K\) directions uniformly distributed unit hypersphere: \[\{\mathbf{d}_k\}_{k=1}^{K} \subset S^{p-1}\] direction \(\mathbf{d}_k\), algorithm proceeds follows: project \(p_k(t) = \langle \mathbf{\Theta}_\mu(t), \mathbf{d}_k \rangle\); find local extrema \(p_k(t)\); compute upper envelope \(U_k(t)\) maxima via cubic spline; compute lower envelope \(L_k(t)\) minima via cubic spline. mean envelope : \[\mathbf{M}_\mu(t) = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{U_k(t) + L_k(t)}{2} \cdot \mathbf{d}_k\] sifting iteration : \[\mathbf{H}_\mu^{(n+1)}(t) = \mathbf{H}_\mu^{(n)}(t) - \mathbf{M}_\mu(t)\] starting \(\mathbf{H}_\mu^{(0)}(t) = \mathbf{\Theta}_\mu(t)\). Iteration continues stopping criterion: \[\mathrm{NMSD} = \frac{\sum_t \|\mathbf{H}_\mu^{(n+1)}(t) - \mathbf{H}_\mu^{(n)}(t)\|^2}{\sum_t \|\mathbf{H}_\mu^{(n)}(t)\|^2} < \epsilon\]

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: multivariate IMF \(\mathbf{C}_{\mu,k}(t)\) characteristic timescale: \[\tau_k = \frac{1}{N_p \Delta t} \int_0^{N_p \Delta t} t' \langle \mathbf{C}_{\mu,k}(t') \rangle_\mu \, dt'\] corresponding mean frequency \(f_k = 1/\tau_k\).

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: Partial sums provide scale-filtered signals: \[\mathbf{\Theta}_\mu^f(t) = \sum_{k: f_k > f^*} \mathbf{C}_{\mu,k}(t)\] contains fluctuations frequencies higher cutoff \(f^*\).

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: dynamical properties chaotic systems can characterized using extreme value theory [4], [8]. reference state \(\zeta^*\) phase space, define negative logarithmic return: \[g(x(\zeta), \zeta^*) = -\log\left[\mathrm{dist}(x(\zeta), \zeta^*)\right]\] \(\mathrm{dist}(\cdot, \cdot)\) typically Euclidean distance.

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: Let \(s(q, \zeta^*)\) \(q\)-th empirical percentile \(g(x(\zeta), \zeta^*)\). exceedances: \[X(\zeta^*) = g(x(\zeta), \zeta^*) - s(q, \zeta^*)\] follow generalized Pareto distribution [9]: \[F(X, \zeta^*) \simeq \exp\left[-\theta(\zeta^*) \cdot X(\zeta^*) \cdot d(\zeta^*)\right]\] \(d(\zeta^*)\) instantaneous (local) dimension \(\theta(\zeta^*)\) inverse persistence (extremal index).

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: Local dimension \(d\) measures number active degrees freedom around state \(\zeta^*\): \(d\) equals fractal dimension averaged attractor; higher \(d\) indicates complex local dynamics; noisy fixed point, \(d \approx m\) (embedding dimension). Inverse persistence \(\theta\) measures trajectory stability: \(\theta = 1\) indicates persistence (stochastic/unpredictable); \(\theta < 1\) indicates persistent dynamics (trajectory tends stay region); \(\theta \0\) indicates persistent dynamics (fixed point slow manifold).

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: exceedances \(X_1, \ldots, X_n > 0\), scale parameter \(\sigma\) exponential GPD estimated maximum likelihood: \[\hat{\sigma} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^{n} X_i\] local dimension : \[\hat{d} = \frac{1}{\hat{\sigma}}\]

title: Chameleon attractors: theory and embedding-EVT-MEMD framework
text: Let \(T_1, T_2, \ldots, T_n\) interexceedance times. Suveges estimator [10] : \[\hat{\theta} = \frac{2\left(\sum_{=1}^{n}(T_i - 1)\right)^2}{(n - N_C)\sum_{=1}^{n}(T_i - 1)(T_i - 2)}\] \(N_C\) number consecutive exceedances (\(T_i = 1\)).

Takens embedding    - Estimate m, tau if not provided (FNN, ACF methods)    - Construct Theta_mu(t) in R^m  2. MEMD decomposition    - Generate K directions on S^{m-1}    - For k = 1, 2, ..., N:        - Sift to extract MIMF C_k(t)        - Update residual    - Compute frequencies f_k = 1/tau_k  3. Full attractor metrics    - Compute d(t), theta(t) for full Theta_mu(t)  4. Scale-dependent metrics    - For each frequency cutoff f*:        - Reconstruct Theta^f_mu(t) from partial sums        - Compute D(t,f), theta(t,f)  5. Chameleon detection    - Analyze variation of <D(t,f)>, <theta(t,f)> across f    - Identify transition frequencies    - Classify attractor type  Output: Metrics, MEMD decomposition, chameleon indicator

text: Given scalar time series \(\{\Theta(t)\}\), Takens’ theorem guarantees dynamics can reconstructed \(m\)-dimensional embedding space via delay coordinates: \[\mathbf{x}(t) = [\Theta(t), \Theta(t-\tau), \ldots, \Theta(t-(m-1)\tau)]^\top\] \(m\) embedding dimension \(\tau\) time delay. package estimates \(m\) using false nearest neighbors (FNN) \(\tau\) autocorrelation function.

title: chamaeleon - Chameleon attractors via Takens, MEMD and EVT
text: MEMD decomposes multivariate embedded trajectory \(N\) intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) ordered decreasing frequency: \[\mathbf{x}_\mu(t) = \sum_{k=1}^{N} \mathbf{C}_{\mu,k}(t) + \mathbf{R}_\mu(t)\] Partial sums reconstruct dynamics frequencies cutoff \(f^*\): \[\mathbf{x}^f_\mu(t) = \sum_{k: f_k > f^*} \mathbf{C}_{\mu,k}(t)\]

(2023): Preprocessing: Optional low-pass filtering isolate dynamically relevant frequencies reduce noise contamination. Parameter estimation: Automatic estimation embedding dimension (m) time delay (tau) provided. Takens embedding: Reconstruction attractor m-dimensional phase space using delay coordinates. MEMD decomposition: Extraction multivariate intrinsic mode functions representing dynamics different timescales. Full-attractor EVT: Computation instantaneous dimension persistence complete embedded trajectory. Scale-dependent metrics: EVT analysis partial sums MIMFs reveal frequency-dependent attractor properties. Chameleon detection: Statistical assessment whether metrics vary significantly across scales. Interpretation results: Scale-invariant attractor: D(f) theta(f) remain relatively constant across frequency scales. attractor uniform geometric properties regardless observation timescale. Chameleon attractor: D(f) /theta(f) vary significantly frequency. attractor appears qualitatively different observed different timescales, indicating complex multiscale dynamics. title: Compute scale-dependent EVT metrics — scale_dependent_metrics
text: key insight chameleon attractor exhibits different geometric dynamical properties different frequency scales. filtering embedded signal retain modes frequency cutoff, can characterize attractor properties change observation scale. Methodology: frequency cutoff f*, algorithm: Reconstructs scale-filtered signal using partial sums MIMFs: $$\Theta^f_\mu(t) = \sum_{k: f_k > f^*} C_{\mu,k}(t)$$ \(C_{\mu,k}(t)\) multivariate intrinsic mode functions frequencies f_k. title: Takens time-delay embedding — takens_embed
text: time series transformed m-dimensional state space via delay coordinate map: $$\Theta(t) \rightarrow \Theta_{m,\tau}(t) = [\Theta(t), \Theta(t-\tau), \ldots, \Theta(t-(m-1)\tau)]^\top$$ suitable conditions (Whitney embedding theorem), reconstruction diffeomorphic original attractor, preserving geometric topological properties. Theoretical background: Takens' theorem (1981) guarantees deterministic dynamical system, delay coordinate map provides faithful reconstruction attractor embedding dimension m > 2*d, d attractor's box-counting dimension. practice, smaller m often suffices. Parameter selection: Time delay tau: small leads strongly correlated coordinates (attractor collapses diagonal). large leads loss dynamical connection coordinates. ACF-based methods find balance automatically. Embedding dimension m: small leads self- intersecting (folded) attractors. large adds noise dimensions. FNN method identifies minimum dimension false neighbors (caused projection) eliminated. Computational notes: core embedding implemented C++ efficiency.
